MEETING HEADER:
Date: 2026-01-12
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Jenna Park (Redwood AE), Elliot Kim (Redwood SE), Aisha Patel (NorthStar - Head of Cloud Partnerships), Martin Reyes (NorthStar - CTO), Lou Chen (NorthStar - Partner Eng)

SUMMARY (auto-gen, may be imperfect):
Quick partner intro between Redwood and NorthStar Infra to explore reseller / infra partnership for dedicated GPU capacity and private deployments. Discussed integration touchpoints (SSO, onboarding), benchmarking approach, potential pilot workloads, and commercial model (rev share vs. reseller + capacity commits). Security and data residency came up; NorthStar asked about SOC2/ISO, KMS, and audit logs. Next step: SE deep-dive and share benchmarking checklist + partner terms.

TOPICS COVERED:
- Partnership model and go-to-market (reseller vs co-sell)
- Technical integration: provisioning, SSO/SAML, customer onboarding
- Infra details: GPU SKUs, on-prem options, VPC peering
- Benchmarking & pilot scoping: workloads, perf targets, cost targets
- Security/compliance: SOC2, ISO, KMS, audit logs

TRANSCRIPT:
00:00 Jenna Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jenna with Redwood inference, AE for partner programs. Super excited to meet the NorthStar team. Who wants to kick us off with a quick intro?
00:12 Aisha Patel: Hi — Aisha here, head of cloud partnerships at NorthStar. We've been talking about doing more partnerships in the LLM infra space, we run managed GPU clusters and also an on-prem appliance. Our sales folks see demand from ISVs wanting a managed private inference option.
00:30 Martin Reyes: Martin, CTO. We're interested in how Redwood handles dedicated and private deployments and how partners can resell or integrate our infra into Redwood Dedicated offering.
00:42 Jenna Park: Great. High level, Redwood provides hosted API, a Dedicated reserved capacity product, and Private with VPC/on-prem options. We surface a consistent API so customers can move between modes. Our partner motion is either resell + capacity, or co-sell with a referral revenue share.
00:59 Lou Chen: Quick question — when you say "private on-prem", is that a full appliance we ship or a control-plane that runs in our cloud? We have customers who can't leave data off-prem.
01:12 Elliot Kim: (SE) Good question. For Private we do a customer-managed control plane option — there are deployments that run the control plane in the customer's VPC with connectors to their infra. For fully air-gapped on-prem we have an on-prem package but it has longer lead times. There's also key management integrations with KMS/HSM.
01:34 Aisha Patel: That HSM/KMS integration is important for a few of our regulated customers. Do you have SOC2/ISO attestation?
01:40 Jenna Park: Yes we have SOC2 Type II and are in the process of certifying ISO-27001. We can share the security pack — it includes audit log examples, SSO/SAML flows, RBAC, and KMS integration notes. I'll send that after the call.
01:56 Martin Reyes: For benchmarks — what do you need from us? We run a mix of LLM workloads, mostly 7B and 13B models for retrieval-augmented generation and real-time chat. Latency is important — tail latency for short prompts is critical.
02:12 Elliot Kim: For benchmarking we'll request instance specs (GPU type, memory), network topology, and samples of request patterns. We'll test with model variants (fp16/quantized) and measure token/sec and p99 latency under the target QPS. We also look at batching and KV cache patterns since that affects cost/throughput.
02:33 Lou Chen: Our infra uses A100s and upcoming H100 fleet, and we also do some inference on sparsely provisioned T4s for low-cost bursts. Is Redwood flexible about hybrid SKU support?
02:46 Elliot Kim: Yes, runtime can route to compatible variants by policy — e.g., low-cost T4 pools for non-latency-critical workloads and H100/A100 for real-time. We also support quantized model variants.
02:58 Aisha Patel: Commercially, partners want clarity on margin and capacity commitments. Are you doing monthly reserved capacity for Dedicated?
03:07 Jenna Park: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with commit terms (monthly/annual). For partners we can structure reseller deals where NorthStar sells capacity and Redwood provides the control plane, or a joint offering where Redwood reserves capacity on NorthStar infrastructure. We can run a pilot to prove economics first.
03:24 Martin Reyes: Pilot sounds right. We want to scope 2-3 workloads and set success criteria around p99 < 200ms for short chat prompts and cost per 1M tokens under $X.
03:36 Elliot Kim: Agree. For pilot scoping we'll capture workload templates, expected QPS distribution, prompt length distribution, and SLOs. We'll also want to run stability tests for 24-72 hours.
03:50 Aisha Patel: On the integration side — our provisioning is via an API we expose to partners, plus SSO via SAML. How does Redwood onboard partner infra?
04:03 Elliot Kim: We ask for provisioning endpoints, SSH/agent access for initial config, and a DNS/VPN handshake. For VPC peering we use standard peering, and we can support private link options. We'll share a checklist.
04:16 Lou Chen: Do you have a partner SDK or terraform modules?
04:19 Jenna Park: We have infra templates and some terraform modules for private on-prem installs; not everything is public but we'll share relevant modules as part of the pilot.
04:27 Martin Reyes: Security again — what about audit logs and tenant isolation? Our customers require per-tenant auditability and ability to rotate keys.
04:35 Elliot Kim: We log token-level metadata, route/tracing hooks, and per-route dashboards. Tenant isolation is supported with dedicated pools or strict namespace isolation in multi-tenant mode. Key rotation is supported via KMS integrations.
04:50 Aisha Patel: Any customer references for partners in similar spaces?
04:54 Jenna Park: We have a few references (engineering-first startups and an enterprise customer in fintech) — I'll include anonymized case studies.
05:03 Martin Reyes: Competitors we see are Paperspace and Lambda Labs; how do you position vs them?
05:10 Jenna Park: We position as production-first inference with strong observability, rollout controls, and cost-performance tooling (batching, caching, quantization recommendations). We also emphasize unified API across hosted/dedicated/private.
05:24 Lou Chen: For the pilot, timeline wise — can we run something in 3-4 weeks?
05:29 Elliot Kim: If we get infra specs and a testbed, yes. The path: share checklist, agree on workloads, spin up pilot cluster, run benchmarks, then review. 3-4 weeks is tight but doable.
05:42 Aisha Patel: One more — support model for partners? Level of SLA for Dedicated?
05:47 Jenna Park: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime/latency tiers for committed contracts. For partners we can provide a co-managed support model with escalation paths; we'll outline support tiers in the partner doc.
05:59 Martin Reyes: Ok — let's recap next steps.
06:02 Jenna Park: Recap: Jenna will send partner one-pager, security pack, and partner terms. Elliot will send benchmarking checklist and required infra spec form. NorthStar (Lou/Martin/Aisha) will share infra topology, GPU SKUs, and sample perf numbers. Schedule SE deep-dive for Jan 19th?
06:22 Aisha Patel: Jan 19th works — we'll tentatively block time.
06:25 Lou Chen: I'll get the topology doc over by Jan 20th.
06:29 Jenna Park: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with those attachments and a calendar invite.
